_note: Inputs for the scalar() agreement check. tools/validate.py and web/lib/_validate.mjs each hold a scalar() that turns a regex-captured YAML scalar into its value. They are the same gate at two different doors: if they disagree, a passport one of them calls valid the other refuses, and the owner gets no message that explains it. web/tools/parity.mjs feeds this list to both and requires identical output.
_why_these: The first four are the ordinary forms. The rest are the ones that actually caught a divergence on 2026-09-03, when the Python side used .strip("\"'") and stripped any number of quotes of either kind from both ends. That is wrong about YAML and wrong in the permissive direction: it made the local validator accept values the endpoint refuses.
